# Non-AWS DNS teardown, 2026-10-04

PROD-LIFE-06 previously stopped every managed GCP, Azure or OCI DNS teardown in `execution/destroy.ts`, even though deployment already used provider-specific target ownership assessors. Teardown now uses those same assessors for the exact supported native DNS types. It reads current ownership while producing the review, while inspecting the saved plan, and after the final human approval lookup before dispatching the original saved plan.

GCP requires the historical managed load balancer, an exact readable project and zone, complete unique forwarding-rule discovery, scoped labels and matching live record values. Azure requires the exact subscription, owned endpoint resources and record tags; Container App routes also retain the existing companion `asuid` TXT ownership and verification-value check, including when the primary record is absent. OCI requires the exact workspace and environment, region and compartment, complete runner responses and uniquely owned public load-balancer identity. Unmapped native types, referenced records, missing historical targets, foreign ownership and unreadable or malformed responses still refuse teardown. The activity exposes a fixed refusal instead of provider values or transport error text.

OCI's existing destroy capability has no DNS GET rule. The activity therefore asks the existing capability broker for a new `infrastructure.plan` read grant for the parent destroy operation and opens a separate `observe` callback through the existing credential broker. This follows `execution/session.ts` and `platform/broker.ts`: the broker loads the current running operation, reevaluates the attenuated capability, checks its environment fence and signs the same principal, proposal and owning scope. `platform/credentials.ts` independently loads the tenant-scoped verified connection and enforces runner capability, region, compartment, current configuration and complete successful job receipts. The activity also compares the returned read claims and session scope with its parent operation and lease. A refused read grant has no fallback. The original destroy grant, write session and raw saved-plan custody remain responsible for the write; an ownership assessment supplies no write authorization.

The change retains the reviewed digest, mandatory human approval, exact deployed resource graph and saved-plan provenance checks. The final DNS read sits after the existing fresh provenance comparison and current approval lookup, before the final fence assertion and original-plan dispatch. Existing independent verification still marks a resource deleted only after a non-simulated `missing` observation. A provider timeout after accepted dispatch remains uncertain, and an inaccessible or simulated read cannot prove absence.

The new focused tests call the real assessors over the existing modeled REST and OCI response fixtures. Their execution ports, plan custody, engine effects, cloud reads and readback are scripted. The OCI fixture uses the actual runner transport serializer and allowlist with each freshly requested capability. It does not prove a native credential broker, real runner job, PostgreSQL authority, Temporal execution, OpenTofu deletion or live cloud permission. A separate AWS control covers the final ownership read after an awaited approval lookup. Existing test callbacks and all provider assessors, sessions, broker contracts, allowlists and shared fixtures remain outside this patch.

No tests, compiler, lint, imports, services, databases, Docker, Temporal, cloud calls or commits were run by the author. Root owns independent source review and serial execution. A focused command for the coherent candidate is:

```sh
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run tests/execution/destroy.test.ts tests/execution/destroy-dns-ownership.test.ts tests/execution/deletion-guards-clouds.test.ts tests/providers/gcp/dns-ownership.test.ts tests/providers/azure/dns-ownership.test.ts tests/providers/oci/dns-ownership.test.ts --no-file-parallelism --maxWorkers=1
```

Root should also run the pinned compiler, scoped lint and the existing real saved-plan destroy acceptance checks. Live GCP, Azure and OCI teardown, real OCI read-job receipts and current customer IAM permissions remain separate authorization and acceptance work. This packet introduces no new required runtime flag, migration, credential authority or provider fallback. Any canonical gate registration and live-provider acceptance are outside the four owned paths.
